title: Finite purely inseparable closures of polynomial rings over normal Japanese domains
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] which is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Let $F$ be the fraction field of the polynomial ring $R[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and suppose $F$ has characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], where $p$ is prime. Let $L/F$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Let K be the fraction field of R and identify Frac(R[x]) with K(x) by clearing finitely many coefficient denominators. The characteristic p of K(x) restricts to K. Choose a K(x)-basis y_i of L and a common q=p^e with y_i^q in K(x). In an algebraic closure of L, choose t with t^q=x and the q-th roots c_j of all coefficients of rational-function numerators and denominators representing y_i^q. The K-algebra generated by the c_j is spanned by monomials with each exponent below q. It is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field K′. Every element has q-th power in K, so K′/K is finite purely inseparable. Taking coefficient roots of each numerator and denominator gives f_i^natural(t), g_i^natural(t). Their q-th powers are f_i(x), g_i(x); the denominator is nonzero. Injectivity of iterated Frobenius identifies y_i with their quotient. Thus L embeds in K′(t) over K(x). The latter extension is finite: adjoining the c_j and t to K(x) adjoins finitely many algebraic elements.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Let A be the integral closure of R in K′. It is a normal domain with fraction field K′. Since K′/K is finite, algebraicity of t over K′ would imply algebraicity of x=t^q over K, a contradiction. Consequently A[t] is a polynomial ring, normal with fraction field K′(t); the last identification follows by clearing coefficient denominators. Let C be the integral closure of R[x] in K′(t). Every element of A is integral over R and hence over R[x], and t satisfies the monic equation T^q-x, so A[t] is contained in C. Conversely an element of C is integral over A[t] and lies in its fraction field, hence belongs to A[t]. Thus C=A[t].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: The Japanese hypothesis makes A finite over R. If a_j are module generators, then the finitely many a_j t^r with 0 <= r < q generate A[t] over R[x]: write each exponent k=qs+r and use t^q=x to reduce a_j t^k to x^s a_j t^r. The argument also applies for q=1.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: The embedding L into K′(t) takes the integral closure of R[x] in L into C, by applying it to monic equations. It is R[x]-linear and injective. Since R[x] is Noetherian and C is finite, its image submodule is finite, and pulling module generators back along this linear equivalence proves finiteness of the integral closure in L.
